predecessors.name: Rouran Khaganate
predecessors.text: the Rouran steppe: 74% of the Göktürk 555 shape (14,281 of 19,248 cells) lies inside the Rouran 554 shape

predecessors.name: Hephthalites (White Huns)
predecessors.text: the Hephthalite land (Transoxiana, Sogdia, Bactria north of the Oxus, Khwarezm, Fergana) that Cliopatria hands from the White Huns 555 shape to the Göktürk 561 shape

successors.name: Eastern Turkic Khaganate (Eastern Göktürks)
successors.text: the eastern half "still ruled from Ötüken", the Mongolian Plateau

successors.name: Western Turkic Khaganate (Western Göktürks)
successors.text: the western half ruled by Tardu, capital Suyab in the Chu valley, from the Tarim basin to the Caspian

ledger.x: 552: Bumin defeats Anagui and proclaims the Turkic khaganate at Ötüken.
552: the Turks and the Rouran fight for the steppe.
553: the Yenisei Kyrgyz under Turkic control.
555: the Rouran steppe is the Turks'.
555: the Turks take the Rouran steppe.
557: Turks and Sasanians move on the Hephthalites.
560: the Hephthalite land passes to the Turks.
560: the fighting for the Hephthalite land ends with the empire destroyed 'around 560 CE'; the Alchon Huns page gives 557-565 for the same alliance, so the end year is approximate.
561: the Turks hold the steppe to the Don.
586: the relation is closed with the state.
586: the eastern half becomes its own khaganate.
586: the western half becomes its own khaganate.
586: the First Turkic Khaganate ends in Cliopatria's reckoning; the page has it split in 581 and formally divided in 603 ('The Khaganate collapsed in 603').

wars.name: Göktürk revolt against the Rouran
wars.outcome: Bumin defeated Anagui in 552 (Anagui killed himself); the Turks occupied the Rouran in 555 and Muqan had the Rouran remnant destroyed.

wars.name: Göktürk-Sasanian war against the Hephthalites
wars.outcome: The Hephthalite empire was destroyed 'around 560'; the Turks took the land north of the Oxus and the Sasanians suzerainty south of it.

wars.name: Göktürk civil war
wars.outcome: The realm divided into an eastern part (Ötüken, Sui orbit) and a western part (Tardu, Suyab); the formal division is 603, with a brief reunification under Tardu 599-603 (Eastern Turkic page).

wars.name: Göktürk campaign in the Crimea
wars.outcome: The Turks crossed the Kerch Strait in 576, besieged Chersonesus five years later and roamed the Crimean steppe until 590; no land is drawn, the shape stops at 37.8 E.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout; no treaty line is dated by the pages.
